Issued at 303 PM CDT Thu Oct 22 2026

A top 10 weather day is unfolding before us as you would probably 
struggle to describe a nicer late October day than what we have. 
Temperatures range from low 70s in western WI and central MN to as 
high as the upper 70s in southern MN as of 2:30pm, with a light 
breezy out of the south to southeast and mostly clear skies. The 
only cloud cover on satellite is over portions of western WI with 
some fair weather cumulus as the rest of the area is under total 
sunshine. Our days are getting shorter so get outside and enjoy the 
beautiful weather while it lasts!

Our last couple 70 degree days will be tomorrow and Saturday as we 
see breezy southerly winds pick up tomorrow ahead of an incoming 
cold front which will bring shower chances and much cooler 
temperatures after it passes. Winds increase to 15-20mph with gusts 
as high as 30-35mph in western MN by Friday afternoon out of the 
south with a few showers also moving across the area due to the 
increased omega from the WAA in the lower levels, as we do maintain 
enough moisture to produce showers. The breezy winds will partially 
elevate fire weather conditions, however the showers moving in and 
the relatively high moisture will keep RH high enough to prevent any 
sort of statement or Red Flag conditions. The rest of the area 
remains dry and enjoys the warmer weather until the front arrives, 
with winds starting to shift in western Minnesota by midday Saturday 
alongside the arrival of more showers along the front. The synoptic 
setup for the front is not ideal for widespread sustained rainfall, 
rather we look to have a line of scattered showers producing rain 
showers with some gaps expected. This is due to a pair of surface 
lows with one moving northwards into central Canada and the other 
down in the southern Plains, with the cold front stretching 
southwards from the northern low. As a result our forcing is rather 
weak even with some omega from WAA ahead of the front as we are too 
far removed from the actual low pressure centers. This line of 
showers looks to stretch from roughly Duluth to Sioux Falls by Noon 
Saturday, with showers weakening into the evening and largely 
dissipating overnight into Sunday. Winds will shift from southerly 
ahead of the front to northwesterly by Saturday afternoon as they 
also weaken below 10mph, with a continued northerly shift by Sunday. 
Weak high pressure tries to slide into the gap left by the front as 
it sags southwards on Sunday, however the southern plains low looks 
to move northeast and push the high off to the northwest as a final 
round of rainfall arrives on Monday morning. This final round looks 
to be the most robust of the group as the surface low weakens but 
moves closer to the area, with southwestern and southern MN favored 
for the highest rainfall amounts which look to range from 1/2 to 3/4 
inch.

Behind the front we return to much more normal temperatures in the 
50s for highs and upper 30s to 40s for lows, which is much closer to 
our normal near 50 degree high temperatures by Halloween. However, 
ensemble guidance is favoring a brief period of above normal 
temperatures again starting Wednesday as another synoptic scale 
system moves across central North America, with a warm frontal 
boundary bringing low level WAA once again. As of right now, this 
looks to be more mid to upper 50s highs with maybe a few 60s, 
instead of the 70s we have been seeing. So while it is a cooldown 
compared to now, it still ends up above normal overall. This warm 
stretch is also relatively short lived, with the cold front from the 
same system moving through by the end of next week and returning us 
to near normal to end the month. We still do not have any indication 
of near freezing temperatures, which means even if we do see 
precipitation chances, we expect to see only rain with little chance 
for any snow.
